newsitem.title: HUNGARY: EBRD offers K&H $30 million financing package.
newsitem.headline: EBRD offers K&H $30 million financing package.

text.p: Hungary's Kerskedelmi es Hitel Bank (K&H) is to issue a $30 million seven-year convertible bond to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) prior to its privatisation.
Hungary plans to sell (K&H), Hungary's third largest commercial bank by assets, by the end of 1997.
"The EBRD's financing is pivotal to our efforts to restructure and privatise within a tight time frame," K&H's CEO Janos Eros said in an EBRD statement.
"On the basis that we are successful in attracting a strong strategic investor we would then hope to seek public listing of our shares by the end of the year."
State privatisation agency APV is expected to publish a tender for the sale of a stake of at least 25 percent plus one vote in the second quarter.
Financial investors would then be invited to raise the capital of K&H by $30 million, subject to the approval of the chosen strategic investor.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) had already expressed its interest in providing the equity increase, which has to be completed by May 31.
One condition of the purchase is that conversion to common equity may only take place once a strong strategic investor has been selected through the government's tender process.

"The EBRD's purchase of K&H's subordinated convertible bond will encourage interest from international investors who would otherwise have been reluctant to invest," EBRD president Jacques Larosiere said.

The EBRD said the structure was different from other bank privatisations in which it has been involved in that it is second tier capital with a long maturity, which is still unavailable to most Hungarian borrowers.
